seo.description: The Paperboat handbook: turn a folder of text files into a website. Install it, write a page, publish.

props.title: Start here
props.text: Paperboat turns a folder of text files into a website. This handbook gets you from nothing to a published page in about ten minutes, then explains each part properly.

items.title: Install it
items.text: Download Paperboat for your computer and open it once. There is nothing to configure.

items.title: Make a folder
items.text: Any folder. Put a file called index.txt in it and write a sentence.

items.title: Press Build
items.text: Paperboat makes a site folder beside yours. Open index.html to see it.

items.title: Publish
items.text: Drag the site folder to any web host. The Publishing page lists five free ones.

items.title: Page
items.text: One text file. Its name becomes its address.

items.title: Layout
items.text: The frame around every page: the menu, the footer, the fonts.

items.title: Build
items.text: Turning your folder into the finished site. It takes a second or two.

props.title: Writing pages
props.text:
A page is a text file. The first line is its title. Leave an empty line between paragraphs.

## Headings and lists

Start a line with ## for a heading and with - for a list item.

- Two stars around words make them **bold**
- One star makes them *slanted*

## Pictures

Put the picture in the same folder and write its file name on a line of its own.

items.a: The first line of the file is the title. If the file starts with an empty line, there is none.
Check the file name matches exactly, capitals included. photo.JPG and photo.jpg are different files.
Yes. Name the file .md instead of .txt and all of Markdown works.

props.title: Publishing
props.text: The site folder is plain files. Anything that can serve files can host it, and most places do it for free.

items.title: GitHub Pages
items.text: Good if the folder is already on GitHub.

items.title: Netlify
items.text: Drag the folder onto their page. Done.

items.title: Cloudflare Pages
items.text: Fast everywhere, a little more setup.

items.title: Your own computer
items.text: For a home network or a classroom.
